analysis:
The supplied PR change to docs/provider/cli-reference.md is documentation only. It bumps the 'Last updated' date (line 3) and adds a head-side paragraph at lines 1577-1588 describing a switch from Date `>=`/`<=` to `timeIntervalSince(_:)` for waits and earnings windows, plus build-time checks (scripts/check-date-comparisons.py, scripts/check-provider-weak-imports.py) against weak Foundation imports on pre-release macOS 27.2. The supplied units (base lines 2487-3074) are unchanged surrounding text: unenroll, logs and refusal lines, report, the paths table, provider.toml keys, the env passthrough list, runtime constants and cluster docs. The changed hunk itself is outside the supplied unit text, so I judged it from the patch excerpt only.

No security-relevant behavior change is visible. The described change keeps limits and results the same, and I saw no change to authorization, attestation (TB-011, T-053/T-054), encryption, prefix-cache storage (T-041), add-on hold (TB-012) or any trust boundary. The new release-build refusal of binaries with weak imports is a build-integrity hardening, not a regression. The docs claim the guard scripts exist; I could not verify them from the supplied evidence, and the code changes behind this documentation are not in this batch.

Remaining integration question: whether the actual code changes (timeIntervalSince in wait and earnings paths, the new scripts) preserve the intended timeout semantics. This is an availability concern only, and it is outside the supplied evidence. No threat-model update appears needed.
